absent: Flush, shrink, barn initialization, node structure initialization, and sheaf cache predicate internals are not shown.
Notifier registration, workqueue use after creation, slab state values other than FULL, and sysfs group layout are not shown.
Object iteration, freelist checking, red marker values, origin size handling, track record layout, and slab address translation are not shown.
Per-node counter maintenance, NUMA fallback behavior, page allocation flags handling, and bitmap helper internals are not shown.
Debugfs file formats, sysfs alias creation, kset and kobject lifetime beyond the release hook, and attribute permission bits beyond read-only versus read-write grouping are not shown.

findings.text: Late allocator initialization creates a per-cpu reclaim-capable flush workqueue and warns when creation fails, then initializes one-shot random state when freelist randomization is enabled.
Memory hotplug notifier entry dispatches first-memory-adding and last-memory-removing actions to online and offline helpers and normalizes the helper result into a notifier code.

Late slab subsystem initialization creates the slab kset and debug root, marks global state full, publishes every existing cache to sysfs, adds user-tracking debug entries conditionally, then drains pending aliases.

Validation service flushes cached per-cpu state, allocates a bitmap sized to the cache order capacity, validates every online node, frees the bitmap, and reports total validated slabs or allocation failure.
Offline transition visits every registered cache, flushes per-cpu state under global protection, shrinks reclaimable slabs, and reports success unconditionally.

Online transition skips caches already having a node structure, allocates barn state only for sheaf caches missing it, allocates and initializes node state otherwise, installs both under global protection, and only then marks the node in slab node masks.
Per-slab counters expose in-use objects and total object capacity directly from the slab descriptor for use by partial-list aggregation.

Validation checks slab identity and freelist consistency before object checks, always walks partial lists, additionally walks full lists only when user tracking is enabled, and compares walked counts against stored partial and total counters.

Tracking aggregation keeps entries ordered by call address then stack handle then waste, merges repeat keys by incrementing counts and widening time, pid, cpu and node coverage, and otherwise inserts in order with capacity doubling.
Slab object statistics deliberately avoid taking the memory hotplug lock while sysfs locks are held because of a documented three-lock order, relying on node data surviving offline transitions.
Global slab mutex serializes walks over all caches and installation of per-node and barn state during online, offline, and late initialization, including updates to slab node masks.
Per-node list lock held with interrupts saved protects iteration over partial and full slab lists and the associated counter consistency checks during validation.

Allocation site aggregate holds a stack handle, occurrence count, call address, waste bytes, summed and minimum and maximum ages, minimum and maximum pids, a cpu bitmap sized to configured cpus, and a node mask.
Tracking table holds a capacity, a populated count, a pointer to a page-allocated aggregate array, and a file offset cursor, with growth preserving existing entries.
Sysfs attribute descriptor pairs a generic attribute with cache-specific show and store callbacks, with container helpers recovering the descriptor and owning cache from generic sysfs objects.
Deferred alias record links an owning cache, an alias name string, and a next pointer in a singly linked boot-time list.

Hotplug handling has two guarded transitions: adding first memory moves a node from absent to initialized per-cache state plus mask membership, while removing last memory moves through flush and shrink without destroying node state.
Subsystem bring-up moves from pre-sysfs to full operation only after kset and debug root creation succeed, with boot caches published and aliases drained before releasing global protection.

Sysfs dispatch resolves generic objects to cache plus attribute, requires the corresponding callback to exist, and otherwise fails access while delegating lifetime release to a dedicated cache release hook.

Online bring-up can fail after processing some caches: barn allocation failure aborts with out-of-memory, node allocation failure releases the just-allocated barn and aborts, leaving earlier caches initialized and later caches untouched.

Validation counter mismatch and invalid slab identity are reported through error logging plus test-error accounting rather than aborting the walk, so callers see a count while diagnostics record corruption.
Tracking table expansion under atomic context can fail when full; insertion then reports failure and drops the new site instead of growing.
Identifier string length limit is 32.
Slab statistic selectors are four ordered values 0 through 3 for all, partial, objects, and total, with one-hot query masks 1, 2, 4, and 8 formed by shifting one by the selector.

Read-only cache geometry and identity attributes report size, alignment, object size, objects per slab, order, sheaf capacity, constructor symbol or empty, alias count derived from reference count, user copy size, and single-bit cache flags.

Slab count attributes share one aggregator with selector combinations for partial slabs, partial objects, all slabs, total capacity, and allocated objects, emitting a total followed by sparse per-node breakdowns.
Legacy per-cpu attributes are fixed compatibility shims reporting zero values, with writes accepting only zero and rejecting nonzero object counts as invalid.

Writable controls validate strictly: minimum partial accepts an unsigned decimal, defragmentation ratio accepts 0 to 100 and stores ten times the value, shrink and validation accept only a leading one with validation additionally requiring debug mode, statistics clear only on a leading zero, and fault injection and KFENCE skip toggles interpret leading zero or one.
Fault injection toggling is rejected when the cache has more than one active user, while other flag toggles apply immediately.
Per-cpu statistics sum one named counter across online cpus and append sparse per-cpu contributions, while clearing zeroes that same counter on every online cpu.

Published sysfs attribute set always includes geometry, partial behavior, and lifetime controls, and conditionally adds debug counts and checks, DMA behavior, NUMA defragmentation, detailed allocator statistics, fault injection, user copy size, and KFENCE behavior.
